subject: ci: add a backend test job, and fix the tests that blocked it (#1935)
message:
ci: add a backend test job, and fix the tests that blocked it (#1935)

Nothing has ever run the Django suite on a pull request - .github/workflows/
holds only lint-*, image-*, docs and mobile-cd. The job could not simply be
added, because five tests fail on dev. Four of them are tests that baked in a
deployment-specific path; the fifth is a coin flip.

test_dirtree (x2) and test_setup_directory hardcode "/data". DATA_ROOT is
os.path.join(BASE_DATA, "data"), so that spelling is correct only when
BASE_DATA is unset or "/", i.e. inside the container. Under the invocation
apps/backend/CLAUDE.md and scripts/setup_test_env.sh document, DATA_ROOT is
/tmp/librephotos/data and all three fail. They now derive the path from
settings.DATA_ROOT, which is right in both places, and create it first -
UserSerializer.update requires the directory to exist as well as to be inside
the data root.

test_face_recognition_client asserted that the raw "<html>service error</html>"
body appears in the exception message. It cannot: _get_response_preview passes
HTML bodies through _strip_html first, and its docstring says why - a Flask
error page should not be dumped whole into a log line. Commit d70d62f9 added
the helper and the tests together, and 0bb44a38 later added the HTML branch
with no test changes, so the assertion has been stale ever since. The test now
asserts the visible text reaches the message and the markup does not, which
also pins behaviour that had no coverage before.

test_stack_review.test_ordering_by_created_at_descending is flaky, failing
about a third of runs: created_at is auto_now_add, the model orders on
created_at alone, and its pk is a random UUID, so two reviews created in the
same clock tick resolve by coin flip. The test now spaces the timestamps
explicitly. Note this is a real property of the model, not only of the test -
StackReview rows created in the same tick have no stable order, so they can
shift between pages. Giving the model a sortable tiebreak needs a migration
and is left to its own change.

Only tests changed; no application code.

The workflow itself installs into a virtualenv rather than the runner's
Python, because setup_test_env.sh falls back to `pip install --user` when

discrepancies that survived an independent verification pass are fixed
here. The conceptual material was largely accurate; what had drifted was
everything operational and referential.

The main themes:

- Post-monorepo path rot. `codedir` is gone from the compose files but
  dev-install.md still called it "CRITICAL"; contribution/index.md told
  contributors to fork "the relevant repository"; backend/missing-photos.md
  cited 20 files under a `librephotos/api/...` prefix that no longer
  exists; contribution/docker.md built with a `docker-compose.gpu.yml`
  that has never been in the repo.

- Redux is gone from both the frontend and the mobile app, but six pages
  still walked contributors through `UploadSlice`, `redux-persist` and
  `redux-query`, and two to-do lists solicited a migration that is done.

- Stale UI labels. "Scan photos (file system)" is now "Scan", the
  favourite control is a star and `f` is bound to favourite rather than
  fullscreen, and missing-photos.md's four resolution paths all named
  controls that do not exist. Labels are now taken from the i18n files.

- ML credits predated the stack: face detection is InsightFace (SCRFD +
  ArcFace), not ageitgey/face_recognition; clustering is hdbscan; CLIP +
  FAISS and SigLIP 2 were missing entirely. offline-setup.md listed two
  models that are no longer in ML_MODELS and omitted Moondream.

- Broken contracts for scripted clients. Media routes and the chunked
  upload endpoints authenticate from the `jwt` cookie and ignore
  `Authorization: Bearer`, which api-authentication.md recommended.

- installation/unified-deployment.md's external-Postgres path could not
  work as written: `DB_HOST=localhost` cannot reach a sibling container
  and `GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE` has not been enough for
  `migrate` since PostgreSQL 15. It now creates a shared network, uses
  the container name, and makes the app user the database owner.

- The env var reference was missing SECRET_KEY, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS,
  FRONTEND_BASE_URL and the DB_* set, and documented ALLOW_UPLOAD twice
  under a plural name that is a silent no-op.

Docusaurus ignores is removed, `excerpt:` becomes `description:` so pages
emit a meta description, colliding sidebar_position values are resolved,
and the User Guide index is no longer a blank page in front of 27
children.

subject: fix: repair the bugs surfaced by the documentation audit (#1940)
message:
fix: repair the bugs surfaced by the documentation audit (#1940)

* fix: repair the bugs surfaced by the documentation audit

While reconciling the docs with the code (#1938), a number of the
"discrepancies" turned out to be the code being wrong rather than the
prose. Each bug here was reproduced with a failing test before being
fixed.

The two serious ones:

- cleanup_deleted_photos filtered `last_modified__gte=now-30d`, so the
  daily retention job permanently deleted the photos a user had most
  recently trashed and kept photos older than 30 days forever. The
  window was inverted. It runs on every install via
  start_cleaning_service in all three container entrypoints.

- createadmin and createuser called User.objects.make_random_password(),
  removed in Django 5.1 while requirements.txt pins 5.2.16, so both
  raised AttributeError whenever no password was supplied. The backend
  and backend-gpu entrypoints hit this whenever ADMIN_USERNAME is set
  without ADMIN_PASSWORD. Replaced with get_random_string(32).

The rest:

- get_count_stats counted other users' missing photos: `Q(owner=user) &
  Q(files=None) | Q(main_file=None)` binds as `(owner AND files) OR
  main_file`, leaving the second branch unscoped. Same precedence fix
  already applied to delete_missing_photos.
- AlbumDateListViewSet appended Q(owner__username=None) when ?public=true
  arrived without a username, so it always returned an empty list. Added
  the guard both sibling viewsets already had.
- PhotoCaption compared CAPTIONING_MODEL/LLM_MODEL against "None" while
  the ChoiceField stores lowercase "none", so selecting None never
  disabled captioning and the LLM branch always ran.
- The Moondream entry in ml_models was selected only by LLM_MODEL, so
  choosing it for captioning never downloaded it and do_all_models_exist
  returned True with the GGUF files absent.
- Three navigations targeted /user/<username>/, which is not a route;
  they now use /public/$users.
- The Duplicate Detection settings card rendered raw i18n keys; added the
  missing translations and dropped dead "Find Duplicates" defaults that
  never rendered.
- Mobile: turning Debug Logging on wrote "Logging: Disabled" and deleted
  the user's log files, which also broke shake-to-send bug reports.
- Mobile: one rejected photo aborted the whole upload batch and left
  itself indistinguishable from never-attempted; SyncStatus.SYNCING was
  declared but never assigned, pinning the Settings counter to 0.
- FEATURE_PROCESS_EMBEDDED_MEDIA was the only feature flag using a strict
  == "True" test, so true/1/yes silently disabled it, and it was never
  wired into compose.

The Stack RAW+JPEG switch is deliberately NOT fixed. DetectStacksView
does drop detect_raw_jpeg, but that is not why the switch is dead: the
grouping moved to scan-time file variants in migration 0112 and now runs
unconditionally without reading User.stack_raw_jpeg, so no change
confined to the view could make it work. Added two @expectedFailure
tests that pin the intended behaviour and will fail as unexpected
successes once it is properly implemented.

Full backend suite: 1702 tests, 4 failures, all four reproduced
identically on pristine dev. Frontend vitest 66 passed, mobile jest 13
passed, ruff and eslint clean.

subject: fix(backend): return the on-disk spelling of a Live Photo companion (#1941)
message:
fix(backend): return the on-disk spelling of a Live Photo companion (#1941)

find_apple_live_photo_video() probes ".mov" then ".MOV" and returned the
candidate path it had just constructed. On a case-insensitive filesystem
Path.exists() matches a constructed "IMG_002.mov" against an on-disk
"IMG_002.MOV", so the function handed back a spelling that no directory
entry actually has.

That matters beyond cosmetics: the scanner records paths exactly as
os.scandir reports them, File.path is unique, and File.create() is a
get_or_create on it. A mis-cased path therefore creates a second File row
for a file the scanner already knows about, and the
File.objects.filter(path=video_path) lookup in
_create_apple_live_photo_stack() misses that existing record.

Resolve the candidate to its real directory entry instead. The lookup is
deliberately not gated on sys.platform: LibrePhotos scan directories are
frequently SMB/CIFS mounts, which are case-insensitive on Linux too. It
costs one listdir, paid only once a companion video has been confirmed
found - i.e. only for actual Live Photos, which already trigger hashing
and database writes - so photos without a companion never pay for it.

Also drop the decorative print()s from test_trash_api.py. They emitted
U+2705 / U+2139, which raises UnicodeEncodeError on a cp1252 console and
turned two passing tests into errors on Windows; they were debug noise
rather than assertions.

subject: fix: give StackReview a monotonic pk so its ordering is a total order (#1944)
message:
fix: give StackReview a monotonic pk so its ordering is a total order (#1944)

Meta.ordering was ["-created_at"]. created_at is auto_now_add, so two rows
written in the same clock tick hold the same value, and with a random uuid4 pk
there was nothing to break the tie - the database was free to return such rows
in either order. Under offset pagination that lets a row move between pages and
be served twice or skipped. #1935 fixed the flaky test that exposed this by
spacing the two timestamps by hand and left the model alone, because changing
it needs a migration.

A uuid4 tiebreak is not enough. It makes ties deterministic but in an arbitrary
order, so it fixes pagination without ordering the tie the way created_at would
have. The tiebreak has to follow insertion order, and Django only allows an
auto-incrementing column as the primary key (fields.E100, "AutoFields must set
primary_key=True"), so the monotonic column cannot be a separate "seq" field -
it has to be the pk. id is now a BigAutoField, and the uuid4 moves to `uuid`, a
unique non-pk column, so rows stay externally nameable by the same value as
before and no sequential counter has to leak into an API.

Reaching a real database sequence through db_default was the other way to get a
monotonic column while keeping the uuid pk, but it is Postgres-only and the
suite runs on SQLite. A unique constraint on created_at instead would turn a
benign tie into an IntegrityError on the write path.

The migration is written by hand. makemigrations generates a bare AlterField
from UUIDField to BigAutoField, which is silently destructive: Postgres cannot
cast uuid to bigint at all, and SQLite's table rebuild would coerce the uuid
strings to integers. Adding `uuid` unique in one step fails from the other end,
since AddField evaluates a default once and writes that single value to every
row. It adds the column nullable, copies each row's old pk into it, applies the
unique constraint, and only then swaps the pk.

StackReview has no serializer, view, url or admin, and no frontend or mobile
reference. Its only callers are two order-independent .filter().update() calls
in api/views/photos.py, so nothing downstream changes and the pagination hazard
this fixes was latent rather than live.

Two things this deliberately does not do. It leaves StackReview inconsistent
with MetadataEdit, which took the uuid4 tiebreak in #1921 and documents it there
as determinism rather than chronology. And it does not touch Duplicate, which
has the same defect and, unlike StackReview, a live offset-paginated endpoint -
DuplicateListView orders by -created_at alone - but which Photo reaches through
a ManyToMany, so the same fix is not cheap there.

Verified on SQLite against a populated database: existing pks survive into uuid,
id becomes a sequence, and same-tick rows come back in insertion order, stably
across repeated queries. Not verified on Postgres.

subject: fix: stop the unified image shipping a stale copy of production.py (#1947)
message:
fix: stop the unified image shipping a stale copy of production.py (#1947)

The single-container image carried a second, hand-maintained copy of the
production settings at deploy/docker/unified/production_noproxy.py, and the
entrypoint pasted it over librephotos/settings/production.py at boot. Nothing
kept the two in step, so the copy fell behind: keys added to CONSTANCE_CONFIG
never reached it, and SiteSettingsView reads them unconditionally.

    File "/code/api/views/views.py", line 125, in get
      out["map_tile_provider"] = site_config.MAP_TILE_PROVIDER
    AttributeError: MAP_TILE_PROVIDER. Did you mean: 'MAP_API_PROVIDER'?

Every unified install answers GET /api/sitesettings with a 500. The frontend
calls that endpoint before login, so the whole UI is down, not just the map.
OCR_MODEL was missing the same way and would have been the next 500 - along
with EMAIL_BACKEND (password reset mailed through Django's default SMTP
backend instead of DynamicEmailBackend), the password_reset throttle rate,
WORKER_CONCURRENCY, and a `photon` map provider that migrations 0093 and 0127
move installs off.

Make it an overlay instead of a fork. librephotos/settings/production_noproxy
imports production and overrides only what running without a proxy changes -
WhiteNoise and the static config, ALLOWED_HOSTS, CORS, CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS,
the security headers NGINX would add, and the DB_BACKEND sqlite/postgresql
switch. That is the same shape development.py and test.py already use, and it
makes this class of drift impossible: anything added to production.py arrives
here for free.

The entrypoint now exports DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE rather than overwriting a
file. Besides being reversible, that drops a sticky-state bug - the old `cp`
left production.py overwritten for the container's lifetime, so a restart with
SERVE_FRONTEND unset kept using the no-proxy settings.

subject: fix: stop the constance admin 500ing on FACE_RECOGNITION_MODEL (#1949)
message:
fix: stop the constance admin 500ing on FACE_RECOGNITION_MODEL (#1949)

CONSTANCE_CONFIG declares FACE_RECOGNITION_MODEL with the custom field type
"face_recognition_model", but that name was never added to
CONSTANCE_ADDITIONAL_FIELDS. ConstanceForm.__init__ tells a named field type
from a Python type with

    if config_type not in settings.ADDITIONAL_FIELDS and not isinstance(default, config_type)

so an undefined name falls through to isinstance("buffalo_sc",
"face_recognition_model") and raises

    TypeError: isinstance() arg 2 must be a type, a tuple of types, or a union

The form is built for the whole config at once, so this took down
/admin/constance/config/ entirely -- on every install, not just ones that had
touched the face recognition setting.

Add the missing ChoiceField, mirroring the sibling model entries. The choices
are the five MlTypes.FACE_RECOGNITION packs in api/ml_models.py, labelled the
way the frontend's selector labels them (SiteSettings.tsx). No "none" entry:
unlike llm_model and ocr_model, face recognition cannot be switched off here.

The regression tests guard the class of bug rather than this one instance:
every named field type in CONSTANCE_CONFIG must be defined in
CONSTANCE_ADDITIONAL_FIELDS, and every such default must be a valid choice of
its own field -- the adjacent failure where the page renders but refuses to
save. The admin changelist test is the actual 500 repro.

subject: fix(backend): never let a failed download land in the model directory (#1950)
message:
fix(backend): never let a failed download land in the model directory (#1950)

`_download_file` did not check the HTTP status, so the body of an error
response was written out as if it were the model. Hugging Face answers a
missing file with a 15 byte `Entry not found` page, which was saved as
`ppocrv6_small.tar.gz` and only surfaced later, far from its cause, as:

    tarfile.ReadError: not a gzip file
    gzip.BadGzipFile: Not a gzipped file (b'En')

For archived models this was merely confusing. For the models stored
unpacked (resnet18, mistral, siglip2, moondream) the error page stayed at
the final target path, where `_model_target_exists` accepts it as an
installed model forever after - a broken install that never self-heals.

- Check `raise_for_status()` before writing anything.
- Stream to a `.part` sibling and move it into place only once the
  transfer completed, so a partial or failed download reaches nothing.
- Reject a body shorter than its content-length, unless requests
  decompressed it on the fly (then the length does not describe it).
- Remove the archive even when extraction fails, so a corrupt one is not
  re-read on the next run.
- Keep downloading the remaining models when one fails, and mark the job
  failed with the reason. `download_models` is chained ahead of scans and
  setup steps, so one unavailable model used to abort the whole chain and
  leave the job stuck reporting "running".

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat: let regular users see their own jobs (#1958)
message:
feat: let regular users see their own jobs (#1958)

Job history was admin-only, so a regular user who started a scan had no
way to tell whether it finished, is still running, or failed. The worker
dot in the header shows the single active job and nothing else, so once
a job ended there was nowhere left to look.

Adds a /jobs page and /jobs/$id detail route for any authenticated user,
listing only their own jobs. Reachable from "My Jobs" in the profile menu
(desktop) and the footer menu (mobile), plus a "View all jobs" link in the
worker-dot popover.

JobDetailView is extracted out of the admin route so both routes share it
via a backTo prop. That mattered: the detail page hardcoded "Back to
Admin" pointing at /admin, which renders "Unauthorized" for a non-admin
and left them in a dead end.

JobList takes a single variant prop ("admin" | "mine") rather than
separate title/detailBasePath/showStartedBy flags. Hiding the "Started By"
column is only correct because the list is narrowed to one user, so as
independent flags a future caller could hide the owner column on an
unnarrowed list and silently misattribute jobs.

On the backend LongRunningJobViewSet.get_queryset learns ?mine=true. The
non-staff branch returns before the parameter is ever read, so a regular
user passing ?mine=false structurally cannot widen their result set. The
frontend only sends the parameter when narrowing, so the admin area's
request is unchanged.

New English strings only; Weblate owns the other locales.

subject: fix: serve media for album-shared photos instead of 500 (#1956)
message:
fix: serve media for album-shared photos instead of 500 (#1956)

UnifiedMediaAccessView still asked for AlbumUser.public, a field that no
longer exists since sharing moved to the AlbumUserShare relation. Django
raises FieldDoesNotExist while building the query, so the defensive
getattr(album, "public", False) on the following line never runs and the
request 500s.

That loop is the "is this photo in an album shared with me?" check, so
every album-level share was broken for media: the recipient sees the
album but gets a 500 on every thumbnail and every original. Unauthorized
requests returned 500 instead of 404. Both the thumbnail branch and the
originals branch were affected, which is why video playback and
"download original" failed too, not just thumbnails.

Both now use the _public_album_active_q() helper that the four other call
sites in this file already use, via a single _may_access() helper.

Also harden the MultipleObjectsReturned fallback. When several Photo rows
share an image_hash it picked photos.first() -- an arbitrary row from an
unordered queryset, possibly owned by a different user -- so the real
owner failed the owner check, fell through to the album branch and was
denied their own photo. _pick_visible_photo() now prefers a row the
requester owns, then one shared with them, then one in an active public
album, before falling back.

The 403-on-missing-or-invalid-token behaviour, the anonymous public-album
path, and the originals branch's inline=True distinction between owner
access and album-share access are all preserved.
